verdicts.proposal_name: P1: Restore/overshoot the idiosyncratic cash-flow band (sigmaj) + ivol characteristic
verdicts.critique:
The INVARIANCE claims are correct and I verified them by reading the code, not by trusting the proposer. sigma_j enters create_arrays only at panel_functions_bgn.py:51-55 (the draw), :61 (corr_zj = beta/(sigma_z*sigmaj)) and :121 (C = exp(Cbar - 0.5*sigmaj^2 + eps*sigmaj)). Because corr_zj is DEFINED as beta/(sigma_z*sigmaj), cov(log M, log C_j) = -sigma_z*sigmaj*corr_zj = -beta_j identically, so E[C]=Chat and the risk-neutral value Chat*exp(-beta) are invariant. Nothing in the investment rule (:82), beta_avg (:148-149), A (:153), G (:157), P (:161-164) or any of the four eret terms (:172-186) touches sigmaj. In sdf_compute_bgn.py the OFF-DIAGONAL cash-flow term is result4 = exp(kron(col2,col2)) with col2 = chi*sigmaj*corr_zj, whose entries are sigma_i*c_i*sigma_j*c_j = beta_i*beta_j/sigma_z^2 -- literally invariant to the band. Only the i=j diagonal correction diag4_add, which carries exp(sigmaj^2) (:246-256), moves. So the change is exactly and only 'inflate the diagonal of Sigma'. Jstar.csv, D(r), beta_star, scale, prob_in_money are all untouched. That is a genuinely clean, minimal, non-rigging intervention and I endorse the direction.

Five objections. (1) THE 'RESTORATION' FRAMING IS FALSE AND THE PROPOSER'S OWN SCAN PROVES IT. git show 2cce11f (2026-06-18) shows the original was `+ 0.3*np.abs(Cbar)`, i.e. m=1.0, cut 10x that day. The proposer's scan reports m=1.0 gives sd(log d)=0.309 and pairwise corr 0.421 -- essentially no improvement over the status quo. The entire gain lives at m=1.75, a 75% OVERSHOOT of anything BGN or this codebase ever used. Do not sell m=1.75 as 'returning toward BGN's own un-multiplied band'; it is a new free parameter, and it should be defended as such.

(2) sigma_j HAS NO ECONOMIC CONTENT WHATSOEVER, so the new d-dispersion is exogenous noise, not a characteristic-linked object. It is an i.i.d. U[|beta|/sigma_z, |beta|/sigma_z + band] nuisance draw per project (:51-55) that affects NOTHING except the diagonal of Sigma. At m=1.75 sigma_j spans roughly [1.59, 3.53] so exp(sigma_j^2) spans 12.6 to 2.7e5 -- d_i is then determined almost entirely by the single highest-sigma live project among ~6, a max-statistic of pure luck that is orthogonal to size, bm, roe, agr and mom by construction. H2 requires d to be char-LINKED; this makes it maximally char-UNLINKED.

(3) THE SPAN NUMBERS ARE AN ORACLE. '{1, log mve, bm, log ivol} = 72.04%' and 'full quadratic = 93.53%' must be computed with the TRUE log d as the ivol column. The econometrician gets a 60-month realized return sd. For per-project cash flows that are lognormal with sigma ~= 2.6, the relative standard error of a 60-observation variance estimate scales like exp(2*sigma^2)/sqrt(60) ~ 10^5: realized volatility is a nearly information-free estimator of d, and d itself jumps by orders of magnitude the month the max-sigma project dies. The 93.5%-vs-72.0% gap is not reachable.

(4) YOU ARE ABOUT TO IMPORT THE KP14 PATHOLOGY, AND THE PROPOSAL NEVER MENTIONS IT despite it being documented in this project's own memory (docs/kp14_size_idio_var.md). d_i ~ sum_j chi_j*exp(sigma_j^2)/P_i^2 ~ num_i/P_i^2 ~ 1/(size*bm-ish), so D^{-1} ~ size and w* = D^{-1}(rp - Bc) tilts toward LARGE firms while every empirically estimated tangency portfolio loads on the size PREMIUM (small). That is precisely the mechanism that produced KP14's negative Sharpes for all three methods with no sign bug anywhere. At d_max/d_min = 4715 the 1/d leg dominates w* completely. There is a live risk that m=1.75 turns BGN into KP14: all Sharpes collapse or go negative and the DKKM-vs-FF comparison becomes uninterpretable rather than favourable.

(5) THE CALIBRATION MATCH IS ONE MOMENT OF A PATHOLOGICAL DISTRIBUTION. At sigma_j ~ 2.6, median project cash flow is exp(Cbar - 0.5*sigma^2) = e^{-7.1} against mean e^{-3.7}: essentially all cash flow arrives as a rare lottery payoff. Matching sd(return)=12.3%/mo, pairwise corr 0.22 and idio share 0.75 simultaneously is real, but skewness and kurtosis are astronomical, roe (op_cash_flow/book) becomes a lottery-outcome char, and the FF 2x3 sort on roe becomes a sort on which firm got lucky last month. That degrades FF/FM -- which flatters the headline ratio for the wrong reason.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly, but the honest ceiling is well below 1.30x and FM gets more of it than claimed. Once you hand the econometrician an ivol characteristic, log d is (by the proposer's own construction) close to linear in log ivol, so FM regressing on [size, bm, log ivol] recovers the numerator AND the log-denominator linearly; the only thing it misses is the RATIO curvature. The proposer measures that residual as 72.0% -> 93.5%, but that is with oracle log d. With a 60-month realized vol of a sigma~2.6 lognormal the ivol column is mostly noise, which pushes DKKM's attainable share DOWN toward FM's 69-72% rather than up to 93.5% -- DKKM has strictly more parameters to burn on a noisy regressor. Worse, FF is not obviously handicapped: a size x ivol 2x3 double sort is a coarse but genuinely nonlinear b/d approximation, and the real-data low-vol/betting-against-beta literature shows exactly such sorts capture most of the inverse-variance tilt. And there is a scenario where the gap goes NEGATIVE: if w* becomes 1/d-dominated and 1/d is unlearnable luck, all three methods degrade toward noise and the ranking is a coin flip, exactly as in KP14. Finally, the DKKM feature map cannot represent a 4700x-range reciprocal anyway: dkkm_functions.rff rank-standardizes the chars and then rank-standardizes the sin/cos features again, so every regressor is capped in [-0.5,0.5] and rank(1/d) = -rank(d) identically -- the basis is monotone-invariant and therefore cannot distinguish d from 1/d at all. The proposal's own mechanism is annihilated by the estimator it is meant to help unless the second rank-standardization is replaced, which Proposal 3 only 'considers'.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the lever, change what drives it. (a) Cap m at 1.0-1.25 (the historical value and mildly above) so cash flows stay economically recognisable, and get the dispersion instead from making idiosyncratic volatility a DETERMINISTIC, persistent, economically motivated function of firm/project observables -- e.g. sigma_j increasing in the project's beta (riskier technologies are also more firm-specific), or a per-FIRM (not per-project) volatility type drawn once and persistent, so d_i is stable, char-measurable, and estimable from a 60-month window. That preserves H2's ratio nonlinearity (b/d is still nonlinear even when both legs are linear) while making 1/d learnable, which is the whole point. (b) Before running anything, compute at a single month: corr(true log d, log of the 60-month realized vol the estimator will actually see) and corr(w*, size). If the first is below ~0.6 or the second is above ~0.7, stop -- you have built KP14. (c) Ship only together with a fix to dkkm_functions.py:110 (replace the second rank_standardize with per-column unit-variance scaling), otherwise the basis is monotone-invariant and cannot express the reciprocal by construction.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2: Project-scale / intangible-capital wedge kappa breaking the rp = a + b/mve + Chat*pi*bm identity
verdicts.critique:
The premise is correct and it is the single most important structural fact in this file. I re-derived it from the code rather than trusting the proposer: P = G + A (panel_functions_bgn.py:161-164), term2 = pi*A*E[D']/D (:176) so term2/P = pi*e_t*(1 - G_t/P), term4 = Chat*pi*book (:181) so term4/P = Chat*pi*bm, and term1, term3 are date-level scalars (:172, :179). Hence eret_i = [pi*e_t - 1] + [(term1+term3) - pi*e_t*G_t]/P_i + (Chat*pi)*bm_i, exactly affine in (1/mve, bm) with a bm coefficient of Chat*pi = 0.024476 at every date. The cross-section of expected returns in BGN as coded is EXACTLY two-dimensional. Any proposal that does not break this identity cannot raise the dimensionality of the premium, which immediately downgrades P1, P4 and (in premium terms) P6. Breaking it via term4 is the right surgical target.

Now the objections. (1) THIS IS A MEASUREMENT-ERROR PROPOSAL WEARING A STRUCTURAL COSTUME. If kappa_j scales cost AND cash flow proportionally, a kappa=2 project is economically identical to two kappa=1 projects; the exercise rule exp(Cbar-beta)D(r) > 1 is scale-free and J* is unchanged because E[kappa]=1. So kappa introduces NO new economic force whatever. One hundred percent of the mechanism lives in the accounting assumption at :144 that book = I*num rather than I*sum(kappa). The paper must say that plainly.

(2) THE INTANGIBLE FRAMING IS INCOHERENT FOR HALF THE FIRMS. Peters-Taylor / Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou intangibles make book UNDERSTATE economic capital -- the wedge is one-sided. A mean-one lognormal kappa gives book OVERSTATING capital for ~half of projects, which corresponds to no accounting mechanism at all. Use kappa >= 1 (e.g. 1 + expensed intangible) and re-normalise I, or drop the intangible citation.

(3) THE MOMENT ALGEBRA IN THE PROPOSAL IS ALREADY WRONG IN AT LEAST ONE PLACE, AND THIS IS THE KP14 SILENT-CORRUPTION CLASS. term5 = kron(col1, col3*integ_Dexpy) (sdf_compute_bgn.py:180-181) is the assets-in-place leg of i crossed with the cash-flow leg of j; at i=j, s=s' both legs refer to the SAME project and each carries kappa_s once, so diag5_sub (:259-265) needs kappa_s^2 -- exactly what it inherits from col1 and col3. The proposal's instruction (step 8) to 'remove one factor' from diag5_sub is an error that would silently bias the diagonal of cond_var with no exception raised, precisely the failure mode already burned into this project's memory for KP14. If a proposal cannot get one of eight terms right in prose, it will not get eight right in code.

(4) LOOK-AHEAD BUG IN THE PROPOSED CHARACTERISTIC. Step 10 defines payout = op_cash_flow/mve with no shift. Trace the indexing: op_cash_flow[t,:] is the date-t+2 cash flow (:124-126 and the comment at :123); create_panel stacks concatenate((zeros(1,N), op_cash_flow)) so panel row month=t carries op_cash_flow[t-1] = the cash flow paid at date t+1 -- i.e. the cash-flow component of xret_t. That is exactly why roe is defined with a .shift() at :237-243. An unshifted payout hands every method next month's dividend. It would produce a spectacular DKKM result and it would be fraudulent.

(5) IT DOES BREAK 'THE BGN MODEL'. BGN (1999)'s headline is that size and book-to-market are sufficient statistics for risk BECAUSE book measures the capital whose cash flows carry known beta. Deliberately severing book from capital repeals the paper's namesake theorem. That may be the right thing to do, but the paper must then describe the model as 'BGN with mismeasured book equity', not as BGN.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM can capture much more of this than the proposal admits, and the model already hands it the ingredients. Once you add payout yield as a characteristic, the new premium term pi*Chat*I*(Lambda_i/mve_i) is LINEAR in a supplied char up to attenuation, so FM's single-coefficient projection captures E[Lambda/mve] with the average shrinkage and loses only the cross-sectional variance of (pi_i - pi_bar)*y_i. That is a second-order interaction, not a first-order span gap. Worse, the model ALREADY contains the interaction FM needs in linear form: roe = op_cash_flow_{t}/book_{t-1} (:237-243) and bm = book/mve (:245) are both existing chars, and Lambda/mve is roughly roe*bm/Chat -- a single pairwise product, the easiest possible nonlinearity, and one that FF's 2x3 double sorts (which are literally designed to capture pairwise interactions) approximate reasonably well. So the honest prediction is DKKM/FM of 1.05-1.15x from this channel, not 1.2-1.35x. The genuinely unspanned part -- the firm-specific optimal shrinkage weight pi_i = s^2/(s^2 + noise_i^2/(num_i*H)) -- is real but small, and it requires num_i and ivol_i as chars, of which num_i is an exact function of chars you already have (see P3) and ivol_i is the unreliable object criticised under P1. Also note that raising cross-sectional predictive R^2 from 0.043% to 0.5% makes estimation HARDER for everyone in absolute terms but does not by itself favour the high-dimensional estimator; the diagnosis's own est3.py result is that with a LINEAR alpha and homogeneous d, OLS-on-6 (0.267) BEATS ridge-RFF-3600 (0.254). Lambda/mve enters linearly. Without P1's heteroskedastic d as a multiplier, this proposal alone plausibly WIDENS FM's lead.
verdicts.salvage: Keep it, but (i) make kappa one-sided and call it 'expensed intangible investment', citing Peters-Taylor, and re-normalise I so E[cost] is unchanged; (ii) do NOT hand the econometrician a clean payout yield -- the whole point is that Lambda is revealed only noisily, so supply properly LAGGED payout at 12/36/60-month horizons and let the estimator do the filtering; (iii) validate cond_var by brute-force Monte Carlo before believing anything: simulate R_{t+1} many times at a fixed t with N=30 and check E[R R'] elementwise against sdf_loop's ER, term by term. Do not accept the analytic edits on inspection; (iv) run the D2 span diagnostic (max Sharpe attainable in the RFF span divided by max Sharpe attainable in the linear-char span, at the true rp and cond_var) BEFORE writing the sdf_compute edits. If that ratio is below ~1.5 the eight-term algebra is not worth the risk. This is the only proposal here that attacks the verified binding constraint (the exact two-dimensional premium), so it deserves the effort -- but only with the Monte Carlo gate.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3: Repair agr, add age/nproj/payout/ivol chars, rescale GAMMA_GRID
verdicts.critique:
Correct in spirit, and the agr and bandwidth diagnoses are real. But three of the proposed characteristics are defective, and one of them is a look-ahead bug.

(1) 'age' IS CROSS-SECTIONALLY CONSTANT. There is no firm entry or exit in BGN as coded: create_arrays gives every one of the N firms the identical opportunity stream from t=0 (chi[range(T),range(T),:] = invest, panel_functions_bgn.py:96-97), no firm is ever born or delisted, and every firm faces the same arrival process. `df.groupby('firmid').cumcount()` therefore returns the MONTH INDEX for every firm -- an exactly constant column within each cross-section. rank_standardize (dkkm_functions.py:57) would resolve it entirely by np.argsort tie-breaking, i.e. it would inject a SECOND pseudo-random persistent column into all 3600 features, reproducing precisely the agr pathology this proposal exists to remove. This is the same defect class as rf_stand. Delete 'age'.

(2) 'nproj' IS AN EXACT ALGEBRAIC FUNCTION OF TWO EXISTING CHARACTERISTICS. book = I*num (:144), bm = book/mve (:245), size = log(mve) (factor_utils.py:72). Hence nproj = num = bm*exp(size)/I identically. It adds zero information. What it DOES do is hand FM a new LINEAR direction spanning a nonlinear function of (size, bm) that FM previously could not form -- an own-goal that strictly narrows the DKKM-over-FM gap. Delete it, or if you want num in the information set, recognise that you are helping the linear benchmark.

(3) 'payout = op_cash_flow/mve' IS A ONE-MONTH LOOK-AHEAD. As traced under P2: panel row month=t carries op_cash_flow[t-1], which is the date-t+1 cash flow, i.e. part of xret_t. The existing roe is safe only because it applies .shift() (:237-243). Any new payout char must be shifted identically.

(4) THE agr FIX IS COSMETIC AND MISDIAGNOSES THE CAUSE. The degeneracy is not a pandas issue; it is that book = I*num with num a small integer (mean ~6) and P(invest) ~ 5%/month, so book literally cannot change smoothly. Over 12 months a firm with 6 projects expects ~0.7 deaths and ~0.6 arrivals, so P(num_t = num_{t-12}) is on the order of 30-40%, not the claimed sub-20%, and the values remain a coarse lattice of small-integer ratios. The economically honest fix is to make investment less lumpy -- many smaller projects per firm, or a higher arrival intensity -- which simultaneously repairs agr, repairs FF's degenerate cma sort (q30 = q70 = 0), and makes book growth a continuous variable. That is a model change, not a characteristic change, and it is the one this proposal should have made.

(5) THE BANDWIDTH RESCALE IS THE RIGHT DIAGNOSIS WITH THE WRONG PRESCRIPTION ORDER, and the proposer half-knows it. Rescaling gamma while dkkm_functions.py:110 still rank-standardizes the features a second time recovers only the sin-folding part: rank-standardization is invariant to monotone transformations, so gamma is a near no-op for ~76% of features. Rescaling gamma is worth doing only jointly with replacing that second rank_standardize by per-column unit-variance scaling (deleting it outright raises the linear share from 49% to 86%, so it must be replaced, not removed).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposer concedes this: standalone it is worth perhaps 1.02-1.05x, and my reading says the sign is not even guaranteed. Three of the proposed additions actively help the linear benchmark: nproj hands FM a nonlinear function of (size,bm) for free; a clean 12-month agr repairs one of FF's seven factors (currently a degenerate 92/0/8 split with literally empty middle portfolios) more than it helps DKKM; and every additional characteristic enlarges FM's span exactly as much as it enlarges DKKM's if the truth is linear in it. The bandwidth rescale is the only genuinely DKKM-only knob, and the independent estimation experiment in the diagnosis found an x8 rescale HURT badly (0.157 vs 0.254) when the truth was low-order -- which, absent P2 or P5, BGN's truth demonstrably is (rp exactly affine in two chars, verified). Applying P3's bandwidth rescale to the CURRENT model would most likely make DKKM worse. It is a multiplier, and multipliers on zero are zero.
verdicts.salvage: Keep: the 12-month agr (as a partial improvement), ivol, properly LAGGED payout at 12/36/60m, lagged bm, and multi-horizon past returns. Drop: age (constant), nproj (exactly redundant, and pro-FM). Add instead: the economically correct fix for agr, which is to raise the number of projects per firm / the arrival intensity so book growth is continuous -- this also gives the cross-section a real size distribution (currently sd(log mve) is tiny because all firms are ex-ante identical Poisson draws). Sequence the bandwidth change LAST, after a model change has been verified by the D2 span diagnostic to put genuine high-frequency content in the truth, and make it jointly with replacing dkkm_functions.py:110. Also adopt the NMAT=1 and finer-alpha-grid recommendations -- those are unambiguously right and cost nothing.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4: Cohort (vintage) common cash-flow factors with age-dependent hedge weights
verdicts.critique:
The stated mechanism does not exist in this model. The proposal's core claim is that 'firm i's exposure to cohort m is phi_m(i) = the value share of its live projects born in window m, which given pi = 0.99 is in expectation a function of firm age: zero for cohorts older than the firm, rising over the next few decay lengths, then geometrically declining.' Every firm in BGN as coded is born at t=0 and never dies (panel_functions_bgn.py:96-97 and :107 -- N identical firms, an identical i.i.d. arrival/death process for each, no entry, no exit, no delisting). All firms have the SAME age at every date, and in the stationary distribution the SAME expected project-age profile. phi_m(i) is therefore not a function of firm age at all; it is pure Poisson-history luck, an unobservable latent vector with identical cross-sectional mean. The 'bump functions of firm age' that the whole argument rests on are constants.

That is fatal in a specific and symmetric way. With N=1000 and idiosyncratic risk diversified, a portfolio's variance is dominated by residual common-factor exposure, so I agree with the proposer that K_eff=24 unpriced cohort factors would genuinely bite -- unpriced common factors are NOT free to leave unhedged in the large-N limit. But hedging requires the exposures to be MEASURABLE functions of the supplied characteristics, and cohort shares are measurable from nothing in the char set. DKKM's 3600 features are functions of (size, bm, agr, roe, mom); none of them carries vintage composition. So neither FM nor DKKM can hedge, both portfolios acquire large uncontrolled cohort exposure, both Sharpes collapse toward the ratio of the premium to the residual cohort volatility, and the horse race becomes a comparison of two noise vectors -- the exact condition (corr(method weight, truth) ~ 0.00) that the diagnosis identified as making the current results meaningless. This proposal would make that worse, not better.

Secondary problems. It does not break the affine identity eret_i = a_t + b_t/mve_i + Chat*pi*bm_i (verified above from :172-186), so the premium cross-section remains exactly two-dimensional -- it adds only unpriced variance, i.e. it strictly lowers max_sr and adds nothing to the signal. It is explicitly conditional on P1 (with the current band there is only ~7% of non-systematic cash-flow variance to allocate). And the implementation is the riskiest in the set: the vintage kernel must be applied as a per-ROW multiplier on kron(col2v,col2v) with the kron row index mapping to (s,s') as row = s*(t+1)+s'; get it wrong and cond_var is silently wrong with no exception, on top of a 15-20% runtime increase in a step that already runs at n_jobs=1 (config.py:40).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and it is more likely to produce a spurious NEGATIVE gap than a positive one. Because neither method can measure cohort exposure, the realised cohort tilt of each method's portfolio is essentially a random draw; whichever method happens to concentrate less in high-loading vintages wins that run. DKKM is if anything the more exposed method, because its ridge-on-3600-features solution is far less stable across months than FM's 7-coefficient OLS, so its month-to-month cohort tilt is noisier. And the one channel the proposer offers for concentration -- that BGN's exercise rule (:82, invest iff exp(Cbar-beta)*D(r_s) > 1, so the beta cutoff is Cbar + log D(r_s)) makes low-rate vintages hold high-beta projects -- cuts the wrong way for the argument: that makes cohort exposure a function of the INTEREST-RATE HISTORY, which is a date-level object common to all firms, not a cross-sectional characteristic. A common tilt is a market tilt and diversifies into the market factor, which FF and FM both already hold. The residual cross-sectional variation is Poisson noise around a common mean, which shrinks as 1/sqrt(num) with num ~ 6 -- small, and unlearnable.
verdicts.salvage: The right version of this idea keeps the extra common factors but attaches them to something the characteristics reveal. Two options. (a) Load the extra common shocks on the project's SYSTEMATIC RISK TYPE rather than its vintage: let all projects with beta in a given band share a cash-flow shock. A firm's exposure is then its value-weighted beta profile, and betabar is recoverable from chars at R^2 = 0.96 -- so the exposures become learnable, hedging them requires a nonlinear function of (size, bm), and FM's L linear coefficients genuinely cannot zero K exposures while DKKM's can. All the analytics survive unchanged because the exponent in E[C_i C_j] stays bilinear. (b) If you insist on vintages, first add staggered firm ENTRY and delisting so that firm age is a real, dispersed, observable characteristic -- which the model badly needs anyway (see missed ideas). Without (a) or (b) this proposal only adds unlearnable noise.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5: Characteristic-dependent clientele demand wedge (AIPT alpha)
verdicts.critique:
This is rigging, and the proposal says so in its own words: 'choose h to be exactly orthogonal, in each monthly cross-section, to {1, size, bm, agr, roe, mom, ...} and to the six FF factor weight vectors, by projecting the candidate h onto those columns and subtracting. Then the FM-attainable Sharpe from the alpha channel is exactly zero and FF's is exactly zero... This is the one proposal where FM cannot capture it is a theorem rather than an approximation argument.' Constructing the data-generating process by projecting out the competitor estimators' spans is not an economic model; it is an answer key. The proposal even anticipates the referee ('the conclusion was assumed') and offers no defence beyond asserting that the alternative proposals do not work. A paper that reports 'DKKM beats FF/FM by 3x' in an economy whose alpha was orthogonalised against FF's and FM's realised weight vectors month by month will not survive a single seminar, and it should not.

The internal-consistency failures are equally serious. (1) THE SDF IS NO LONGER ANYONE'S MRS. Firms exercise growth options at the rule exp(Cbar-beta)*D(r) > 1 (:82) derived from the representative agent's M, and Jstar.csv values those options under the same M, but traded prices are P*W. So the manager maximises a value no shareholder faces, and the reported max_sr and sdf_ret are the MVE of an SDF that prices nothing anyone optimises against. (2) THE 'TRUE' MVE BECOMES THE MODELLER'S INSERTED NEAR-ARBITRAGE. rp and cond_var recomputed with the wedge yield an annualised max Sharpe of ~3.7 that grows without bound in N (alpha'D^{-1}alpha ~ N*E[alpha^2/d]), and nothing in the model prevents anyone from taking it. Koijen-Yogo and Gabaix-Koijen demand systems do NOT produce unexploited near-arbitrage of that magnitude; they produce price impact against ELASTIC arbitrageur demand. Citing them while omitting the arbitrage-capital constraint that bounds the wedge is using their names, not their economics. (3) THE WEDGE IS SELF-REFERENTIAL. h is a function of chars, but mve = P*W so bm, size and mom are all contaminated by W, and h is then orthogonalised against those contaminated chars -- a fixed point that must be solved each month and whose solution depends on the exact char list, so the 'result' changes if a co-author adds a characteristic. (4) 'THESE ARE SIMPLE ECONOMIC MODELS' DIES. The paper's entire framing is that three standard, disciplined production models fail to reproduce the virtue of complexity. Bolting on a hand-designed mispricing function to manufacture the result inverts the paper's claim into 'we can produce the result if we assume it.'
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Yes -- trivially, by construction, which is exactly the objection. The theory diagnosis is right that an unspanned premium is necessary (span2.py: RFF/linear ceiling is 0.994 under exact factor pricing and 21 with nonlinear alpha plus heteroskedastic d), so SOME version of this ingredient is unavoidable. But note two things that undercut even the rigged version. First, the wedge is only partially learnable by design (SIGMA_U is set so the wedge contributes ~15% of idiosyncratic variance), and DKKM must estimate a function orthogonal to every linear direction from 360 months with a feature basis whose participation-ratio effective rank is 14-16 -- the realised DKKM share of max Sharpe could easily be 0.2-0.3 rather than the projected 0.5-0.8, in which case even the rigged economy delivers a modest ratio. Second, at S* ~ 1.1/month both reported metrics degenerate: E[sdf_ret] -> Rf and sd(sdf_ret) -> 0, so HJD converges to ~Rf for every method, and the mean-of-ratios Sharpe is dominated by months where the interpolating alpha=0 column produces a near-hedged w_t with a tiny denominator. The proposal would very likely produce an enormous, unpublishable, metric-artefact-laden table.
verdicts.salvage: A demand wedge is defensible; THIS demand wedge is not. Three non-negotiable changes. (i) Delete the orthogonalisation. Specify h from an economic primitive -- e.g. a benchmarked institutional clientele whose demand is a smooth function of index membership and size, or a tax/dividend clientele -- and then MEASURE how much of the resulting alpha FF and FM span. If they span most of it, that is the finding, and it is an honest one. (ii) Close the model on the arbitrage side: put a finite-capital, risk-averse arbitrageur in front of the wedge so the equilibrium alpha satisfies a capacity constraint and the maximum Sharpe does NOT grow with N. Without that the economy contains an arbitrage opportunity that no agent declines, which is a modelling error, not a friction. (iii) Report the rational and wedge components of rp separately, state that max_sr is now the marginal investor's bound not the representative agent's, and switch to the scale-free pricing metrics (sqrt(1 - rho_uncentered^2), or alpha'Sigma^{-1}alpha from compute_pricing_errors.py) before running anything at S* > 0.5/month. And retitle: this is no longer a simple economic model, it is a model with an assumed behavioural wedge, and the paper's claim must change accordingly.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6: Heterogeneous project durability (discrete survival types), optionally with larger |BETA_ZR|
verdicts.critique:
Economically the most respectable proposal in the set -- heterogeneous asset duration is a genuine, well-documented force, and it is BGN-native (BGN's firms are portfolios of heterogeneous projects; making them heterogeneous in decay as well as in risk is a natural second dimension). The technical claims check out: pi enters D(r) via sum(pi^k * b) (vasicek.py:49-55), Jstar via inner_sum's pi^arange(1,401) and the 951-maturity outer sum (vasicek.py:113-119), and prob_in_money through D (vasicek.py:66-67), so beta_star and scale must be re-fit and Jstar.csv re-solved per type -- the proposer is right about the cost, and right that it is the only proposal requiring a solfile re-solve. Given the KP14 experience with a stale G_func.csv solved under superseded parameters, that alone is a strong reason for caution.

But the payoff is small by the proposal's own arithmetic (DKKM/FM 1.05-1.18x) against the largest cost in the set (M^2 = 9x on terms 3, 5 and 7 of an O(N^2) loop that already runs at n_jobs=1, config.py:40), and there are three substantive problems.

(1) THE BETA_ZR TARGET CONTRADICTS ITS OWN STATED RATIONALE. The proposal says 'real term-structure premia are roughly a third of equity premia in Sharpe terms' and then sets corr_zr = -0.55, giving lambda_xi = -0.22/month. The model's total equity max Sharpe is 0.26/month; a third of that is ~0.087/month, implying corr_zr ~ -0.22, not -0.55. As proposed, the bond factor would carry a monthly Sharpe of 0.22 -- roughly 0.76 annualised on a duration bet, far above any documented term premium.

(2) RAISING |BETA_ZR| CANNIBALISES THE PREMIUM CROSS-SECTION. The SDF's total price of risk is pinned at |lambda| = sigma_z = 0.4 (log M = -r - 0.5*sigma_z^2 - sigma_z*nu; panel_functions_bgn.py:34-36 splits nu into orthogonal xi and mu with lambda_mu = sigma_z*sqrt(1-corr_zr^2) and lambda_xi = sigma_z*corr_zr). Moving corr_zr from -0.175 to -0.55 cuts lambda_mu from 0.394 to 0.334, a 15% reduction in the only channel that generates cross-sectional premium dispersion (98% of sd(rp) comes from A_mu*lambda_mu). You are shrinking the signal to add an exposure dimension. Net effect on the horse race is ambiguous at best.

(3) THE DURATION MIX IS NOT MEASURABLE. Same objection as P4. A firm's type mix is a point on the M-simplex determined by which types it happened to draw; the proposal's identifying signals (payout yield, agr volatility, past-return beta on rate changes) are all extremely noisy in a firm with ~6 projects and 5%/month investment, and two of them (agr volatility, rate-change beta) are not in the char set and would have to be added -- at which point they also enter FM's linear span. The proposal's own risk list concedes that if the types are near-ordered by payout yield alone, FF's size-by-payout double sort recovers most of the mix; avoiding that requires deliberately choosing type-specific parameters so that no single characteristic orders the types, which is a soft form of the P5 rigging.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Probably not at a magnitude worth the re-solve. Two counter-arguments. First, A_xi is already 97.5% correlated with 1/mve, and firm-level duration is a value-weighted average over ~6 projects, so the cross-sectional dispersion of the mix around its common mean shrinks as 1/sqrt(6) and will be substantially collinear with size and bm (both of which already proxy for the assets-in-place share A/P = 1 - G/P, which is itself the main determinant of rate exposure). FM with size and bm will capture most of the duration tilt linearly. Second, if BETA_ZR is left alone, the rate factor is nearly unpriced (|lambda_xi|/lambda_mu = 0.178), so duration heterogeneity is an unpriced-factor hedging problem -- which, per the P4 discussion, does bite at N=1000 but only if the exposures are learnable, and here they are barely learnable for anyone. Third, and decisively for the paper's stated goal: type-weighted term2 and term4 DO break the exact affine identity, but only by replacing bm with a duration-weighted book measure -- the premium cross-section goes from exactly 2-dimensional to about 2.3-dimensional, not to the high-dimensional, densely-signalled truth the virtue-of-complexity theory requires. This buys a fraction of what P2 buys at ten times the cost.
verdicts.salvage: If you do it, do it as M=2 (not 3), leave BETA_ZR alone (or move it to corr_zr = -0.22, consistent with the proposal's own one-third-of-equity-Sharpe target), and add a regression test that the M=1 special case reproduces the current moments exactly before touching anything else. But the far better use of the same idea, at zero solfile cost, is to put the heterogeneity in the PRICED dimension rather than the decay rate: decompose each project's beta_j into K orthogonal priced components (log M loads on several shocks, cov(log M, log C_j) = -sum_k beta_kj), keeping the TOTAL beta distribution exactly as calibrated so the exercise rule, prob_in_money, beta_star, scale, D(r) and Jstar.csv are all literally unchanged. The off-diagonal cash-flow moment stays analytic because the exponent remains bilinear -- sdf_compute_bgn.py:184 becomes exp(kron(col2a,col2a).data + kron(col2b,col2b).data), five lines. That raises the rank of the systematic covariance from 2 to K+1 with persistent, partially char-measurable firm-level exposures, at essentially no cost and with no recalibration. If you want a second dimension in BGN, take that route, not the durability route.

missed_ideas: EX-ANTE FIRM HETEROGENEITY IN THE INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITY SET -- the single largest omission. In BGN as coded every firm is literally identical ex ante: N firms, all alive from t=0, each drawing one candidate project per month from the same beta distribution with the same arrival and survival probabilities (panel_functions_bgn.py:44-46, :81-82, :107). The entire cross-section is Poisson luck around a common mean, which is why sd(log mve) is tiny, why num has mean ~6 and range 1-14, and why the truth is only 2-dimensional. Give firms a persistent latent 'opportunity quality' type -- a firm-specific arrival intensity lambda_i, or a firm-specific location of the beta menu, or a firm-specific project scale -- drawn once and slowly mean-reverting. This costs nothing analytically (all moments remain the same lognormal/Vasicek forms), requires no solfile re-solve if the cross-sectional mean of the menu is held at the calibrated value, and creates exactly the ingredient the diagnosis says is missing: a persistent latent state that the characteristics reveal only NOISILY and PARTIALLY, so recovering it is a nonlinear filtering problem in (size, bm, agr history, roe history) rather than a linear projection. This is also the honest fix for agr's 91% tie mass and for FF's degenerate cma sort.

OPERATING LEVERAGE / FIXED COSTS -- the classic production-based mechanism, absent from all six proposals and analytically FREE here. Give each project (or each firm) a fixed operating cost F per period, so the payoff is C_j - F. Every moment the code needs stays closed form: E[(C_i-F)(C_j-F)] = E[C_iC_j] - F(E C_i + E C_j) + F^2, so sdf_compute_bgn.py's term4 needs only two extra rank-one corrections; the risk-neutral value of the project becomes (Chat*exp(-beta_j) - F)*D(r), still analytic. The economics is exactly what the model lacks: the effective cash-flow beta becomes beta_j*Chat*exp(-beta_j)/(Chat*exp(-beta_j) - F), a NONLINEAR amplification that is large for low-profitability firms and small for high-profitability ones, and idiosyncratic variance is amplified by the same factor. So b(x) AND d(x) both become genuinely nonlinear in roe and bm, and the ratio b/d becomes doubly nonlinear -- H2 with economic content, unlike P1's i.i.d. sigma_j draw. This has enormous independent empirical support (Carlson-Fisher-Giammarino 2004, Zhang 2005, Novy-Marx 2011, Donangelo et al. on labour leverage) and it breaks the exact affine eret identity that P2 targets, but through a real force rather than an accounting assumption. Cost: the exercise rule becomes (Chat*exp(-beta) - F)*D(r) > I, so integrand_optval / integrand_optval_sq (sdf_compute_bgn.py:48-84) and Jstar must be re-derived -- but these are closed-form expressions in the code, not a numerical PDE solve, so this is hours, not the days P6 requires.

TIME-VARYING PRICE OF RISK. sigma_z is a constant 0.4 (config.py:196), so BGN has a constant price of risk and therefore no conditioning channel at all -- which the pipeline audit independently flagged as blocker #6 (KP14 and GS21 have no time-varying input to the feature map; BGN gets one only by accident, via rf_stand being column-stacked raw at dkkm_functions.py:92-96). Making sigma_z,t an AR(1) correlated with r_t makes the optimal weight a function of characteristic x macro-state INTERACTIONS, which is exactly the channel through which complexity is supposed to pay in KMZ/DKKM and which a single ridge coefficient vector applied to unconditional chars cannot express, while a rank-standardized RFF over chars plus a macro-state column can. One caveat the proposals would need to handle: sigma_z enters phi1 and sigma1_sq in the Vasicek recursion (vasicek.py:29, :41), so bond prices, D(r) and Jstar are functions of it -- a stochastic sigma_z requires re-solving on a grid in sigma_z, which is real work. A cheaper variant with the same effect: keep sigma_z constant but make corr_zr (hence the SPLIT of the price of risk between the cash-flow and rate factors) time-varying, which rotates the cross-sectional premium ordering over time without touching the total |lambda| or the bond-pricing recursion.

STAGGERED FIRM ENTRY AND DELISTING. There is no entry or exit anywhere in create_arrays -- N firms exist from t=0 forever. That is why 'age' is unusable as a characteristic (P3 and P4 both assume otherwise), why the size distribution is a compressed Poisson cloud rather than the heavy right tail of real equity markets, and why the model cannot speak to the microcap channel that the DKKM paper shows carries a large share of the real-data virtue of complexity (their Sharpe falls from 3.7 full-sample to ~1.6 in mega/large caps). Adding staggered entry with a heavy-tailed initial scale and a delisting hazard is cheap, is a prerequisite for any age-based mechanism, and directly targets the 'fat left tail of small, high-idiosyncratic-volatility, high-alpha names' item that the theory diagnosis ranked as a real-data feature the models lack.

REPORTING LAGS, STALENESS AND ROUNDING IN THE CHARACTERISTICS -- the cheapest defensible way to make the truth unlearnable-by-linear-methods. All five characteristics are currently exact, contemporaneous, noiseless functions of the latent state (bm = I*num/P exactly, roe exactly, size = log P exactly). Real book equity is reported annually with a 3-6 month lag, is stale between reports, and is measured with error. Simply reporting book at an annual frequency with a lag (and adding a small measurement error) converts the 'chars invert the state exactly' property -- which the diagnosis identified as the reason a small model is the correctly specified model -- into a genuine filtering problem where the optimal weight depends nonlinearly on the age of the last report interacted with recent returns. Zero new economics, zero new parameters beyond the reporting calendar, no solfile re-solve, and it is what real data actually looks like. Notably, none of the six proposals touches the observation process at all except to ADD characteristics.

A PRE-REGISTERED ACCEPTANCE GATE BEFORE ANY sdf_compute EDIT. Four of the six proposals (2, 4, 5, 6) were never simulated, and three of them require delicate edits to the eight-term analytic second moment in sdf_compute_bgn.py -- the exact failure class that silently corrupted KP14 (memory: kp14-zero-capital-sdf-corruption, and the shipped integ_results.npz returning exact zeros with no warning). The gate should be: (i) compute mean_t max_sr_t (already produced by every sdf_loop at sdf_compute_bgn.py:326-328 and saved in *_moments.pkl, but never propagated into results.pkl by evaluate_sdfs.py) and report every Sharpe as a fraction of it; (ii) compute the D2 span ratio -- max Sharpe attainable in the configured RFF span divided by max Sharpe attainable in the linear-char span, at the TRUE rp and cond_var, no estimation -- and require it above ~1.5 before writing a line of moment code; (iii) validate any modified cond_var against a brute-force Monte Carlo of E[R R'] at N=30 and a fixed t. No proposal here includes such a gate, and P2/P4/P6 are all one indexing slip away from the KP14 outcome.

A COMBINATION TEST NOBODY PROPOSED: the diagnosis's own span2.py results say heteroskedastic d is worth ~0.2% ALONE but multiplies an unspanned premium by 1.9x (linear alpha) to 6.4x (nonlinear alpha). That means P1 is worthless without P2 (or a non-rigged P5), and P2 is likely NEGATIVE without P1 (est3.py: with a linear alpha and homogeneous d, OLS-on-6 at 0.267 BEATS ridge-RFF-3600 at 0.254). The correct minimal package is therefore P2's premium channel + a char-LINKED version of P1's heteroskedasticity + fixed operating costs to make both legs nonlinear -- and none of the six proposals is scored as a package. Any single-proposal Sharpe prediction in this set should be distrusted for that reason alone.
